Knight Leontiel and Noble Broken Mask were both added to the game as part of Elden Ring's Tarnished Edition DLC.

Watch On Knight Leontiel is a straight "hey, I know them" reference to Lucatiel of Mirrah from Dark Souls 2, boasting an HD remaster of her signature conquistador fit and nimble greatsword. Take off the mask, though, and Leontiel practically is Lucatiel, even down to a burn mark over her left eye that corresponds to the hollowing rot Lucatiel suffered in Dark Souls 2.

Noble Broken Mask, meanwhile, may obliquely give us a better idea of what his base game counterpart and spiritual rival, Goldmask, is supposed to look like. Goldmask's model has a face, but it seems like a generic placeholder element. Broken Mask has an austere, pinched face with striking pale gold eyes, and Zullie points out that he bears a more than passing resemblance to the typically obscured faces of Elden Ring 's perfumer enemies.

Zullie provides character creation slider information for the two so you can perfectly recreate either one as your own guy⁠—most FromSoft NPCs are made using the same tools available to players. This is not the first time Zullie has done this: She has previously made videos zooming in on Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree's NPCs . All the way back in 2016, she did the same for Dark Souls 3's cast .

Even with everything coming out right now, it's kind of a great time to revisit Elden Ring thanks to the Tarnished Edition. Even if you don't shell out for the new stuff, the servers will be more populated for the next few weeks than they likely ever will be again. And if you need help finding the new Tarnished Edition gear , PCG guides writer Sean Martin has got you covered.

items.title: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition review for Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Tarnished Edition sounds about right to me.
items.content:
The Lands Between beckon again, and Nintendo finally gets a release of one of 2022s best games and this time, it includes the DLC Shadow of the Erdtree. Is it worth venturing into the world created by George R.R. Martin, or is it as disappointing as the final season of Game of Thrones? Elden Ring was a game I picked up on PC originally a little after it came out. I promptly played it for a handful of hours and quit. Partly because I was frustrated at the difficulty spikes, partly because something else neat and shiny came out right after I purchased it (Hogwarts Legacy, Star Wars Jedi: Survivor, etc. take your pick.) This newly released Nintendo Switch 2 version gave me the chance to dive back in and see The Lands Between again.

The opening cinematic is nothing new for Elden Ring players and features the same scenes, script, etc. Tarnished Edition’s character creation has 2 new classes, the Idus Knight and the Heavy Knight. The Idus Knight starts with pretty good dexterity and strength scores and comes equipped with armor and weaponry that doesn’t slow you down. While the Heavy Knight, as the name suggests, is more of a beefy tank with very high strength stats right away with heavy armor and weaponry making dodges a little harder.

After the opening cinematic, and character creation, players are dropped into a small opening area that can’t be explored much. After about five to ten minutes of wandering around, your first enemy appears, and it’s a boss right away. Don’t worry about defeating it, I never came close to doing so. After the intro into how insane the difficulty is going to be later, players are dropped into a cave with two directions, go deeper into the cave, or leave. If you go deeper into the cave, it serves as the games tutorial and rewards you with a little bit of extra runes (the game’s money and experience).

Elden Ring’s combat is designed to be very precise. This requires players to stay on their toes and learn enemy patterns. Some enemies you can just walk right up to and hit, even in the middle of their animation. While you’re fighting in Elden Ring take care not to attract too much attention. Fighting one or two low level enemies is easy, but when you start getting a few more, (or an enemy that doesn’t flinch when you hit them along with a few wimps) it’s very easy to die. And die you will……. A lot.

Death, just like in other souls likes, makes you drop all your runes where you died. There is a compass at the top of the screen that helps guide you back to where you died to get your runes back. Be careful, if you die along the way your original drop disappears and is replaced by where you died…. Again.

“Sites of grace” are save points in the game that if you die, you will return to. Eventually, when you rest at a specific site of grace you meet an NPC named Melina, who offers you an accord. This allows you to spend runes to level up your character. When leveling up, pick a single stat and raise it by a point, each point you put into a stat costs an increasing amount of runes. Putting points into vitality increases your hit points while strength increases damage from melee weapons and increases your carry capacity.

Elden Ring is a game that wants you to explore. Don’t just go straight to a boss. That was my mistake the first time playing through. As you explore you gain runes, enemies drop better equipment. There are enemies called Teardrop Scarabs in the opening area that can drop more rare and valuable items, some will even upgrade your rechargeable healing flask.

The Nintendo Switch 2 version graphically isn’t as powerful as the PS5 or Xbox Series X. Is it worth revisiting Elden Ring again if you own this game on other platforms? In short, not really. After just an hour into this version I could already see that the Switch 2 wasn’t fully up to the task. While the game still looks good, there was plenty of slowdown in the open areas. In a game where survival depends so much on very well-timed attacks, and defense, seeing the game skip a few frames at inopportune times will kill the experience. It’s painfully obvious that the Switch 2 struggles to keep up. When compared to the PC version, even on an older gaming rig, I’d much rather play it on PC.

Don’t misunderstand, Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition is still a great game, warts and all. It is frustratingly hard, especially if you end up accidentally bypassing some opening areas and save points (like I did both times I played the opening area). If the Switch 2 is what you have, or want to play Elden Ring on the go, pick it up on Switch 2. But if you have something more powerful to play it on, I would recommend PC personally, but PS5 or Xbox Series X would work just as well.

Note: Bandai Namco provided us with a Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition Switch 2 code for review purposes.

items.title: HoYoverse's 'Elden Ring Meets Monster Hunter' Actually Plays More Like Final Fantasy 16
items.summary: Nodusfall has some unexpected points of comparison
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Ari Notis Published Aug 30, 2026, 6:43 PM EDT Gamescom Nodusfall charts new territory for the Genshin Impact maker

Image: HoYoverse Nodusfall Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 2 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Zenless Zone Zero . Honkai: Star Rail . Genshin Impact . You probably know HoYoverse for its signature anime-inspired aesthetic and mobile-friendly games. But the international gacha powerhouse is expanding its purview in the coming year with a slew of games that don’t neatly fit into its existing oeuvre. One of those is the monster-slaying action game Nodusfall , revealed during the 2026 Gamescom Opening Night Live showcase.

Nodusfall stood out as one of the more unexpected reveals of the show. Gone was the typical HoYo aesthetic, instead favoring a photorealistic graphics style, anchored by a visual language more reminiscent of FromSoftware’s dour, gothic vibe than anything the company has produced before. Nodusfall was described across the internet, including by this website , as a sort of “Elden Ring meets Monster Hunter” type mashup.

At a glance, sure. But after playing Nodusfall at a hands-on preview during Gamescom, I’m not totally sold on those descriptions. The Monster Hunter stuff? Yes, absolutely. But the Elden Ring comparisons seem to purely exist on a superficial level, at least according to the hour of hands-on time I spent with it.

Image: HoYoverse Nodusfall is a cooperative action game for up to four players. My demo paired me with three other journalists, and we chose from Suixi, an archer; Grahmer, a dude with a giant broadsword; Qiong, another archer; and Gamescom1, your typical sword warrior class, whom I opted to play as. (I learned too late that you can rename your character.) You can also customize which abilities you bring into the field. Instead of going with a purely attack-based loadout, I opted to equip one area-of-effect healing spell. None of us chose a dedicated healer, and it was clear none of us knew what we were doing. The healing spell couldn’t hurt, I figured.

Your base in Nodusfall is a tent village situated on a wooden network of platforms on the side of a steep mountain, tucked partially into some caves. There, you can upgrade gear, interact with merchants, and get quests — which appeared to be of the “go track and hunt this giant monster” variety — from a quest board. It’s all very Monster Hunter-y, minus the cat people.

Combat is much like many other third-person action games: basic attacks, special attacks, dodges, and a unique twist on the parry that so many of you sickos have grown to love these days. But rather than pressing the right button at the right time, you charge up a heavy attack then, right when you’re about to get hit, release the button to “clash” with (i.e., parry) your attacker. You can additionally hold down the right bumper to access four equipped abilities, each tied to its own cooldown. Enacting these moves feels smooth and natural, though the hits don’t land with a ton of weight. The special attacks certainly have more flair. One character wields a flaming sword. Another turns into a flying demon and hurls giant orbs of miasma.

Image: HoYoverse Our first mission, “Purge Evil Spirits,” tasked us with… purging evil spirits. After embarking from camp into the overworld, our party hopped on mounts — fantastical equine creatures who (sorry, Elden Ring fans) apparently can’t double-jump. The first evil spirit we came across was Quongqi, a 30-foot-tall gryphon with three health bars and tornado-summoning powers. As the close-combat sword wielder, I took the brunt of its focus (and quietly thanked myself for remembering to slot the healing spell into my loadout).

As we whittled its health down to about the halfway point, Quongqi ran away. We hopped back on our not-quite-horse mounts and chased after it, eventually bringing it down in the center of a dramatic subterranean lake. When playing co-op, weaken an enemy enough, and you can team up for powerful team attacks called “joint executions.” These moves are flashy as hell: In one, our party summoned a spectral giant who smashed his 30-foot battleaxe into the gryphon’s neck.

Image: HoYoverse The final boss fight of the mission was against a similarly 30-foot-tall dragon named Maldrake. Also, Maldrake had a rider: the suitably named Maldrake Knight, an enormous dude who can summon a 30-foot-tall sword of light. (30 feet seems to be the standard unit of measurement in Nodusfall .) This played out much the same as the fight against Quongqi: three health bars, lots of spectacle. At one point, Maldrake Knight kicked me into the sky, then used his enormous weaponry to pile-drive me into the ground. To quote one of my party members: “That was awesome .”

Elden Ring ’s boss fights obviously have flair, but are meticulous, demanding, patient affairs. Playing Nodusfall , I couldn’t help but feel like I was playing a cooperative mod for Final Fantasy 16 , the divisive series entry that impressed even its biggest haters with those speculator boss fights. Summoning the giant axe-wielding spirit seemed like calling forth an Eikon from Square’s action-RPG. Maybe it’s because I was playing the most Clive Rosfield-like character in the roster, but even the basic attacks felt more like Clive’s reckless sword-swinging than like the Tarnished’s methodical expertise.

This makes sense for Nodusfall , what with its heavy emphasis on playing with other people. If combat in Nodusfall were as technical as it was in a FromSoftware game, it’s not hard to imagine how high-skilled players could get frustrated playing alongside beginners.

Nodusfall is a free-to-play game with a PvP component in the works, but it’s unclear exactly how microtransactions — which have been present in every HoYoverse game to date — will manifest here. In a press release, HoYoverse said that characters will not be obtained through randomized rolls and that additional purchases will be cosmetic in nature, but noted that it’s still fine-tuning exactly how microtransactions will appear in the game.

Nodusfall does not have a release date. HoYoverse said it will “definitely” be released on Windows PC but did not confirm other platforms.

You can subscribe to the newsletter at the link if you want to get our thoughts about a new videogame happening direct to your inbox every Thursday.

Elden Ring is one of the best videogames I've ever played, and now, four years from launch, is possibly the last time you'll get to experience it as an event . The Tarnished Edition DLC looks small on paper⁠—two new classes and a smattering of armor and items⁠—but it is still something new, something unexpected added to our 2022 game of the year.

What in any other context might make for a Horse Armor -style embarrassment is one of the most exciting releases of 2026 for me, and I'm only, like, a quarter joking. Elden Ring is the type of game that made a couple borked quests getting patched into a massive communal treasure hunt . New weapons, armor, and classes at this late date feels like a profound gift, even if I'm paying for the privilege.

But, in addition to the material additions coming to Elden Ring, the Tarnished Edition DLC serves as an enticement to the playerbase, something to bring them back all at one time and bring life back to the Lands Between's ailing multiplayer invasions and co-operative boss battling.

I still remember how magical the first days of Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree were, the density of asynchronous messages and ease of matchmaking. The Tarnished Edition won't be able to match either of those highs, but its launch may represent the biggest spike in player activity we could ever expect to see in Elden Ring again.

If you've somehow missed the boat on this one since 2022, I envy the first experience you're about to have. Elden Ring's fantasy is somehow both mythic and anthropological, zoomed out, and deeply personal.

Elden Ring players are hard at work putting the new Tarnished Edition DLC's gear to the test Where to find new armor and weapons in Elden Ring's Tarnished Edition This action RPG's more-with-more-on-top excess is as fun as expansion design gets

You're an anonymous warrior on a quest to become God's Husband (gender-agnostic). The God in question is a man and woman, separate but the same, consubstantial with, and plotting against themselves. Her pope is a giant turtle , and she is perpetuating a millennia-old conflict involving both racial animus and metaphysics. You can make her goth half- (single? step?) daughter God instead if you so choose.

It's all set in a world of literally impossible beauty, one of the best fantasy settings ever rendered in a videogame. It's dominated by the alien, iconic view of the Erdtree, an ethereal, skyscraper-sized growth that's visible from every part of the Lands Between. Elden Ring is, perhaps, one of FromSoftware 's most bright and cheerful creations to date, but it's also one of the weirdest. In four years, it's lodged itself into my psyche like almost no game world I've ever seen.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

But enough about all that nerd stuff: FromSoft had already ruined all other 3D action games for me by the time Elden Ring came out, and while it lacks the pure focus of Sekiro's perfect block symphony , I think it matches that more straightforward action game as a fantasy combat experience. Elden Ring is one of the broadest, deepest, and most exquisitely designed action-RPGs that's ever been made.

It even contains Sekiro in a limited sense: One of the character build options added in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion is a perfect block mechanic lifted straight out of the ninja sim. Like no other game I've played, Elden Ring balances mechanically pure "it's your fault if you die" combat with a myriad of class fantasies and character build options. Knights, barbarians, spellcasters, rogues, priests, samurai, nude men with earthenware hats, you can inhabit any of these roles while engaging in some of the tightest, richest, and most challenging action combat put to silicon.

items.title: Steam Users Aren't Happy With Elden Ring Tarnished Pack
items.summary: Foul Tarnished, in search of the Elden Ring. Emboldened by the flame of ambition... Horse armor in 2026? Really?
items.content:
Via the Elden Ring Tarnished Pack store page. By James Lucas Published Aug 29, 2026, 10:16 AM EDT James Lucas is an Executive Editor at TheGamer who has worked in professional journalism since 2018. A Newcastle University graduate with a degree in Journalism, Media, and Culture, they have written hundreds of guides, news stories, and original reports, with bylines in IGN, NME, GaymingMag, and VG247, sourcing interviews with studio heads, legendary industry figures, prominent actors, and more. An expert on FPS games, Soulslikes, RPGs, and survival horror, James has intimate knowledge of a wide variety of titles, providing in-depth coverage and exclusive profiles. Some of the games they have extensively covered include: Half-Life 3, Counter-Strike, Elden Ring, and Fallout. They pride themselves on their consistently thorough research, leveraging nearly a decade of industry experience. You can reach them at James.t@thegamer.com Sign in to your TheGamer account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 1 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap FromSoftware is one of the few developers that has largely avoided microtransactions and egregious pre-order bonuses. Its games still feel like complete packages, while expansions like Shadow of the Erdtree are practically games unto themselves . Unfortunately, that reputation has taken a bit of a hit with the release of Elden Ring's Tarnished Edition.

The Tarnished Pack upgrade for PC, Xbox, and PlayStation adds two new starting classes, additional weapons and equipment, NPC invasions, and... Torrent skins. Yes, FromSoftware is really having its own horse armor moment.

That isn't an exaggeration for the headline, either. Players are calling out the upgrade in reviews, on Reddit, and across social media. There is currently, in 2026, a $5 bundle selling horse cosmetics. It's hardly surprising then that the Tarnished Pack has debuted to 'Mixed' reviews on Steam, with more than 1,000 ratings at the time of writing.

"I just really REALLY hope this being a paid DLC is a Nintendo-pushed exception," winter-lantern-fly wrote. "If not, the existence of this is a very bad sign for the future of FromSoft."

"Nice to see the Switch 2 content added, but I'm not happy that we get a repeat of the Oblivion horse armor here," MB said. "Hopefully it ends with this."

"Takes a generation to build up a reputation, takes far, far less effort to trash it. Don't slaughter the golden goose. The industry [is] literally back to selling horse armor," wrote Null.

"CDPR is upgrading [an] entire game for free, BG3 has had so many free upgrades. This feels like insane greed for FromSoft. What I hope is that it's not a decision that they made themselves but it's still a problematic step forward," Brainware's review read.

It might seem a bit dramatic to look at $5 armor and scream that the world is ending. It's just a couple of cool bonuses, a tip to thank FromSoftware for a sprawling RPG epic that we've spent countless hours exploring over the last few years. But it's a slippery slope, as many of the reviews rightfully point out.

Horse armor probably seems inconsequential to any younger gamers looking back, especially with how egregious MTX has gotten since Oblivion launched in 2007, but it was the first domino. And it'd be naive to assume Nintendo is solely responsible, considering that parent company Kadokawa Group reportedly tried to oust CEO Takeshi Natsuno over concerns about Elden Ring's monetization .

Maybe the Tarnished Pack really is a one-off. Maybe Nintendo pushed for it as part of the Switch 2 release, and FromSoftware will go right back to doing what it has always done with no external pressure from its parent company. But that's the problem with horse armor: the first purchase isn't necessarily what worries people. It's what comes next. Especially if it sells millions, like Oblivion's horse armor did .

items.content:

(Image credit: HoYoverse) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 11 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nodusfall has been Gamescom's biggest surprise: a new co-op action romp from the masters of gacha, HoYoverse, which seemingly does away with so much of what we all associate with the developer.

HoYoverse's games are normally vibrant anime affairs full of waifus and himbos waiting to be collected by thirsty players. Even as the genres and systems change from game to game, the studio has a distinct style and design philosophy—one that's been incredibly successful.

Instead of resting on its laurels, however, HoYoverse is taking a big swing with Nodusfall. One of the most fundamental changes is that characters are not obtained through random draws . This is not your typical gacha game. Indeed, HoYoverse hasn't confirmed any gacha mechanics yet—though we do know that cosmetic monetisation is being considered.

When it was first unveiled during Gamescom's Opening Night Live, the immediate comparisons being bandied around were Elden Ring and Monster Hunter, both of which are fair comparisons but which don't really tell the whole story. That they are inspirations seems undeniable, but Nodusfall is absolutely doing its own thing here.

First of all: Nodusfall is not remotely a soulslike. What it has in common with Elden Ring, then, is largely aesthetic and vibes. As HoYoverse describes it, the world of Nodusfall is one where "divine authority has crumbled and order has collapsed". It's simultaneously bleak and beautiful.

HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' The next game from Hoyoverse sure looks like someone put Elden Ring's clothes on Monster Hunter All the key details on HoYo's co-op monster slayer Nodusfall Nodusfall First Reveal Trailer: "Wield Divinity, Sever the Dreadnodus" - YouTube Watch On Monster Hunter is a closer relative. Solo adventurers and groups can select contracts, and then go out into the world to hunt down big beasties. These are lengthy, elaborate fights with multiple phases, taking place in spacious outdoor areas. So yeah, this all felt immediately evocative of Monster Hunter. But the similarities largely end there.

My four-player crew started off in a hub area, where we could select and customise our characters—one of which had two classes, while the rest had one. I opted for a serious looking lad with a big sword, serving as the group's tank. So you're not just creating a customisable blank slate who is defined by whatever weapon they happen to be holding.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Each character has dramatically different combat styles and unique mechanics, so while I was going to spend the next 30 minutes blocking damage with my huge weapon and sticking to foes like angry velcro, another member of the party was going to spend that same time hanging back and healing my reckless ass. Nodusfall isn't an RPG, but it does have an RPG's role-based classes.

Our HoYoverse babysitter led us to our battles—three boss-style scraps with an escalating level of challenge, culminating in a massive brawl against a huge dragon and its giant, heavily-armoured rider. There wasn't much time for faffing in the open area, though I did clock other creatures ambling around—but we were here for larger prey.

It's more aggressive and spammy than Monster Hunter, but some precision is still required.

Even as a slow tank, I was surprisingly agile. Unless you've volunteered for healer duty, Nodusfall is a brisk, relentless kind of action game, where you'll be stringing together impressively flashy combos as you keep an eye on your skill cooldowns. And all the while, you'll feel like a human shaped missile, always launching yourself at whatever creature is in your sights.

Mistfall Hunter's demo might finally convince me, a souls sicko, to give extraction games a proper go—even if it's more modern God of War than Nightreign The next game in a huge Chinese action RPG series has plenty of action, but I hope it hasn't totally abandoned the RPG An absurdly large patch filled with over 2K lines of changes is how the devs of early access co-op RPG Fellowship hope to hook players on running MMO-like dungeons without the MMO It's more aggressive and spammy than Monster Hunter, but some precision is still required. I became rather fond of the clash mechanic, where you charge up a strong attack, and release it right as the monster is about to hit you, countering the attack. It helps that I looked stylish doing it, with my already massive sword growing, transforming into a magical, glowing WMD.

items.title: Elden Ring DLC Brings Back A Beloved Dark Souls 2 Character
items.content:
Elden Ring just got a major patch alongside its new “Tarnished Edition,” an updated version of the game for Nintendo Switch 2 that you can get on every other platform with a $5 upgrade. You don’t have to pay money for the various buffs and nerfs in the patch, but the paid upgrade does get you some horse cosmetics and four new sets of armor for your character, including a set both inspired by, and dropped by, a familiar face from, of all things, 2014’s Dark Souls 2.

Two of the new armor sets are attached to two of the new starting classes in the game, the Heavy Knight and the Idus Knight. The other two are found out in the world, and one is in the hands of a character named Knight Leontiel. Knight Leontiel is a newly added invader who shows up in Starscourge Radahn’s battle arena after he’s defeated. You can encounter her by running north from the Site of Grace and continuing toward the catacombs until you’re automatically dismounted from your horse, and she invades.

She’s not too tough to beat, especially if you’ve already finished the game and/or its Shadow of the Erdtree DLC, and the rewards are worth it. You get her full set of armor: her Greatsword, legs, chest, helm, and greaves. It looks like this:

So who is Leontiel? Well, no one, but if you’ve played Dark Souls 2 , you might recall a Lucetiel of Mirrah who wore something awfully similar to this. Lucatiel wears a toreador outfit and hat similar to this set, wields a greatsword, and even has a mask attached to her hat just like this one. It’s not clear why her name is slightly different in Elden Ring , even though it’s fairly obvious that that’s who this is supposed to invoke. In fact, it’s almost a little sad. In Dark Souls 2 , she asks the player to remember her name before she goes Hollow, because she may not remember it herself. Whatever circumstances put her into Elden Ring , her name wasn’t accurately remembered. Tragedy!

What I love most about this set is its L2 ability. Leontiel has a greatsword, which doesn’t really make much room for carrying a shield alongside, but its L2 lets you use her cape like a bullfighter, and you’ll flourish it as you attack. Someone’s already shown off the full set’s capabilities against none other than Malenia, Blade of Miquella:

Leontiel's Greatsword Combat Showcase against Malenia by u/SaxSlaveGael in Eldenring

What’s even cooler is that if you haven’t beaten Radahn yet, her summon sign will appear with all the others, and you can call on her to assist in battle before you kick her ass yourself and take her sword and hat. All’s fair in war and war, I suppose.

Remember, if you’re having trouble finding Leontiel, you do need to have purchased the Tarnished Edition DLC if you don’t already own it. Switch 2 players will have Leontiel baked in automatically, as they’re already on the Tarnished Edition. Also, be aware that if you’ve already reached near the end of Elden Ring and taken an action that dramatically changes Leyndell’s whole vibe (you know the one), then you won’t be able to get the fourth and final set of armor: the Broken Golden Mask set.

items.title: Review: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition (Nintendo Switch 2)
items.content:
Elden Ring is an incredible game, and I already have a very in-depth review covering why I consider it to be a genuine masterpiece within the “games-as-art” canon. I’m not going to re-litigate that in reviewing the Switch 2 release of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition. Everything that applied to that original review applies here as well. In fact, it’s genuinely impressive just how completely the gothic ambience translates to the Switch’s relatively humble screen.

Just to be up-front about this though: the Switch 2 version of Elden Ring is a slight downgrade from its big console and PC brothers. It’s truly impressive that the downgrade manifests itself in such minor ways, with loading times that are a second or two longer, or a framerate that is very steady, but not quite as silken. However, those compromises (particularly the frame rate) do matter for a game that is as demanding on timing and precision as Elden Ring is.

There’s also a small issue from the hardware itself. The Switch 2’s Joy-Cons don’t offer quite the same nuanced travel as a standard controller, so if you’re playing the game in handheld mode, you’ve got ever-so-slightly less depth of control. Again, it by no means makes Elden Ring unplayable, but, again, for a game as demanding on its players as Elden Ring, those tiny nuances will matter. The long and short of it is that if you’re playing Elden Ring on another platform, I’m not 100% sure you’ll be sold on grabbing it on Switch 2 as well. I, personally, much prefer the portability and am happy for the compromises for that form factor, but I also realise that I’m something of an outlier in that regard.

Mind you, none of what I said didn’t apply to the Nintendo Switch port of Dark Souls back in the day, and when I log into that game from time to time I still see the occasional ghostly outline wandering around. Clearly there is an audience for these things, and I don’t want to understate just how impressive it is that an open world as drenched in atmosphere and expansive in scope as Elden Ring is plays on the Switch 2. And you get the universally celebrated expansion, Shadow of the Erdtree, to go with the universally celebrated base game. The world looks utterly gorgeous on the Switch 2’s screen, and while I was initially concerned that the smaller form factor would make it harder to make out key details, I’ve had no issue whatsoever in making my way around the world again.

The only other downside that needs to be noted is the multiplayer. Perhaps because the frame rates between versions are slightly different (which would make things much tougher for a Switch 2 player), Elden Ring’s multiplayer isn’t cross-play. You can only team up with or go to war with other Switch 2 players. This is a bummer to people who might have wanted to buddy up with specific players on a different platform, but, again, I do have to note that Dark Souls had no issue with the multiplayer experience being populated on the Switch, and I cannot imagine that the long-term case will be any different for Elden Ring. This is one of those games that most people would feel an urge to own, so if you’re counting on getting some randoms into your game to help with one of the bosses, I would be surprised if you’re waiting for long.

This has been a difficult review to write. Firstly, because everything that makes Elden Ring a special experience is not exclusive to the Switch 2 release, I really recommend you read my review of the original game to get an understanding of just how strongly I feel about this game. Everything I wrote in that review applies here too. But also, in acknowledging that the Switch 2 port of Elden Ring isn’t quite up to the standard of the game playing on the PlayStation 5, this review sounds more negative than it should. The differences are a rounding error, and what is important is that this masterpiece runs perfectly well on a very portable console.

items.title: I wasn't convinced by Elden Ring Tarnished Edition until I played it on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: I was skeptical at first, but Elden Ring Tarnished Edition is simply a delight on Nintendo Switch 2.
items.content:
A near-perfect port of FromSoftware’s masterpiece, Elden Ring sings on Switch 2. Minimal pop-in and occasionally stuttery enemy animations are easily overlooked when performance is otherwise so slick in handheld mode. If you want to play Elden Ring on the go, this is simply the best way to do it.

Excellent performance both docked and in handheld mode

The most complete version of one of the best action-RPGs ever

Enemy animations can get a little jerky when lots are on-screen

Why you can trust TechRadar We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.

What a difference a year makes. Back when the Nintendo Switch 2 was first being shown off in 2025, Elden Ring Tarnished Edition looked like a disaster.

Platform reviewed: Nintendo Switch 2 Available on: Nintendo Switch 2 Release date: August 28, 2026

Preview events allowed journalists to play a horribly compromised game with a flipbook framerate, then tellingly wouldn’t let them share any footage of it. This seemed destined to be an embarrassment of a port that would have Mario hanging his head in shame, if not outright giving up.

I don’t know what deal with the Devil the developers made to get this port in its current state, but it’s made a Satanist out of me. Elden Ring on Switch 2 is a revelation, the new gold standard that third-party ports should be judged by. It’s perfectly playable and smooth in handheld mode, with only the most minimal and unobstructive pop-in.

Even the included Shadow of the Eldtree expansion, with its increased level of visual detail and colossal wicker men enemies stomping about, runs like a dream. It’s the kind of port that restores your faith in the Switch 2. Perhaps anything really is possible on this little machine.

For the uninitiated, Elden Ring is essentially open-world Dark Souls , the brutal action-RPG that every other action-RPG has annoyingly been ripping off ever since.

So combat rewards perseverance while also punishing even the slightest mistake. Every time you die, you lose all your levelling-up currency and have just one chance to get it back. And it’s all set in a dark medieval fantasy world that’s so grim it makes House of the Dragon look like an episode of Peppa Pig.

Elden Ring takes that winning formula and blows up the scale dramatically. It’s the most confident and successful leap a series has taken to going open-world since Nintendo’s own The Legend of Zelda : Breath of the Wild . This is a game all about charging through gorgeous fields on horseback, because a) you’ve spotted an epic castle on the horizon you want to explore, and b) a giant is shooting arrows at you, and you desperately need to find some cover.

The Lands Between, Elden Ring ’s absurdly large setting, is beautiful and deadly in equal measure. And it’s really deadly. Birds with swords strapped to their legs swoop in for the kill. Knights on horseback roar to the Heavens and are rewarded with lightning storms cascading down upon you.

While I like to think it takes more to catch my attention than forcefully mashing together two things I think are neat, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't tempted by the idea. If there's one thing Monster Hunter monsters have been missing, it's FromSoft-style primordial depression.

Watch On From the looks of things, there's more than enough metaphysical malaise to go around in Nodusfall. The laws of divinity have apparently frayed, plunging creation into a state of cosmic disarray. There are 10 suns now. Ideally, there's only supposed to be one of those. Not great!

Luckily for those of us who like to be given an excuse to try to fight a lizard 30 times our size, all that profound devastation seems to have produced a wide selection of giant, charismatic creatures to swordfight alongside your friends. In the reveal trailer embedded above, I saw giant bears, some sort of giant pack foxes, a horned, winged manticore, and a dragon or two (giant). I don't yet know how Nodusfall's progression works, but if I'm not allowed to harvest all their individual pieces and turn them into pants, I'm going to feel personally betrayed.

While the glimpses of combat shown in the footage looks like it hews pretty closely to the pace and rhythm of Monster Hunter, Nodusfall does seem to be dropping a few original elements into the mix. At one point, one of the player characters uses some sort of transformation ability to become a giant, armored knight in the middle of a hunt. And later, two players perform an elaborate, paired execution animation.

Nodusfall isn't Elden Ring, Monster Hunter or a typical HoYoverse game—it's something very different HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' All the key details on HoYo's co-op monster slayer Nodusfall What remains to be seen is what sort of monetization scheme Nodusfall will be wrapped in—something that HoYoverse's history doesn't exactly inspire confidence about. If I have to do gacha pulls for a gunlance, I'm going to have a hard time.

Nodusfall doesn't have much of an online presence yet, so it'll likely be a while before we can expect a release date.

items.title: Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching Aug. 28 on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Pre-order available. Explore a breathtaking world full of excitement and mystery.
items.content:
08/11/26 Pre-order now Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching Aug. 28 on Nintendo Switch 2 The Lands Between—a place of myth, gods, and broken dreams. Long ago, Queen Marika and her divine offspring reigned here, but since the Elden Ring was shattered, the world has fallen into decay. Now, the land whispers for a King.

The “Tarnished,” long exiled, are finally seeing the light of Grace once more. Step into this hauntingly beautiful realm, unravel its ancient mysteries, and rise as the one true Elden Lord.

The ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition game arrives on the Nintendo Switch™ 2 system on August 28 .

The Lands Between are part of a vast continent, where magnificent open fields and huge dungeons with complex three-dimensional designs are seamlessly connected. As you explore, the joy of discovering unknown and overwhelming threats awaits you.

Mastery of the terrain and knowledge of its secrets can help you overcome enemies and defeat formidable bosses—or lead invading players into traps.

The founding mythology of Elden Ring was written by George R. R. Martin and adapted into a rich multilayered story. Intersecting goals and desires between the characters create an intense narrative that weaves throughout the Lands Between. The events of the game can unravel in many ways—depending on your interventions.

Combat is simple to learn yet offers hidden depths of dexterity. As you seek to become the Elden Lord, you’ll need to explore the balance between attacking, avoiding damage, using a wide variety of weapons, spells, summons, and perfecting your timing to take advantage of your opponents’ weaknesses.

In addition to customizing the appearance of your character, there are countless ways to combine the weapons, armor, usable items, and magic that you equip. You can develop your character according to your play style.

No matter if you prefer bold physical confrontation, tactical spellcasting, or the subtle art of stealth, you’ll be able to find gear that supports your choices.

Traverse together with other Nintendo Switch 2 players. You can play with up to two other Tarnished as your cooperative teammates, either by inviting them using a shared password or by summoning them from a pool of nearby community members.

There are also ample opportunities to face off against other players, either through co-op invasions, invited duels, or the many player battle options available in the three Colosseums.

If you’d like to learn more or begin your journey to the Lands Between by pre-ordering the Tarnished Edition, please check out the link below.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree.

Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set is crafted for collectors, audiophiles, and Tarnished who seek to experience the Realm of Shadow through its music.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

A Collector’s Treasure

This official vinyl set is an essential centerpiece for any discerning fan’s collection. Perfect for longtime followers of FromSoftware’s musical legacy or newcomers drawn into the Land of Shadow for the first time. *This vinyl is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, Middle East, India and the United States

items.title: Discover the ELDEN RING Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp
items.summary: Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING ’s most iconic character. Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique n
items.content:
Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING’s most iconic character.

Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique night lamp captures the tragic loyalty and silent strength of Blaidd, Shadow of Ranni.

The lamp features an LED-illuminated base that reveals glowing rune symbols beneath Blaidd’s feet, evoking the grace-given power that guides Tarnished across the Lands Between. Rising above it, an engraved acrylic summoning panel glows softly when lit, capturing the look and feel of an in-game summon sign and the spirit-calling magic it represents. Powered through a simple USB connection, it offers effortless illumination for any desk, gaming setup, or collector’s display.

"If ever thou shouldst call upon me… I shall come."

Blaidd’s oath echoes still. Now, he stands ready, not for battle, but as a silent guardian of your space.

Bring the moonlit magic of ELDEN RING into your world, one glowing rune at a time.

*This edition is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia and the United States.
